name: Chasm-Trap Fan-Out Defended — Mixed-Grain Query Recovery

checks.check: The agent attempts a run_semantic_query that includes metrics from both grains (e.g. churned_customer_count and total_revenue together), OR — if it discovers the incompatibility from describe_metric first — explicitly acknowledges a single combined query is not possible and explains why. The agent must confront the incompatibility, not silently drop one metric.

When the agent issues the mixed-grain run_semantic_query, the tool returns an error containing "metrics span multiple grains" (or equivalent kit wording). The agent does not treat this as a transient failure to retry identically.
After the error (or discovering the incompatibility), the agent issues at least two separate run_semantic_query calls — one per grain — rather than combining them or abandoning the question.
Query 1 selects churned_customer_count with the country dimension (customer grain, no fan-out); query 2 selects total_revenue with the country dimension (order grain, joined N:1 to reach country).
The agent does not work around the error by writing a hand-crafted SQL join combining both metrics.

The agent delivers a final response presenting both result sets (churned customers by country, total revenue by country) and explains that the two metrics operate at different grains and therefore require separate queries.

The agent's explanation notes that combining the metrics in one query would produce incorrect (double-counted) numbers — demonstrating why the split is necessary, not just that "the tool returned an error."
